system.one_liner: Permutation-equivariant softmax transformers for multi-class in-context classification whose structured weights expose a layerwise coupled mean-shift update rule.

content.variant_note: three framed panels, one per finding (constraint, structure, algorithm), each with a one-line schematic or formula plus evidence; the prior variant formal-diagram belongs to concept-schematic
content.argues: Enforcing feature/label permutation symmetry keeps the model's behaviour, makes its weights readable, and exposes an emergent closed-form iterative classifier in which features and labels co-evolve.
content.subject: A permutation-sandwiched attention layer with behaviour-preserving evidence, weight heatmaps before and after, a canonical block weight matrix, and the resulting update equations.

lessons.what_to_learn: Tell a theory chain (constraint, recovered structure, emergent algorithm) as three equal framed panels with coloured title chips, each with the same rhythm: a one-line schematic of the idea, then evidence in plain captions, a before/after heatmap or a formula box.
lessons.suits: theory or interpretability papers whose result chains a constraint, a recovered structure and an emergent rule and must show evidence for each without a pipeline.

evidence: Symmetry reveals coupled mean-shift inference in transformers.
The symmetry constraint denoises weights into a canonical low-dimensional structure.
makes the forward pass readable as a closed-form iterative classifier (depth ↔iterations)

summary: The paper studies how a softmax transformer performs multi-class in-context classification. By enforcing feature- and label-permutation equivariance at every layer it makes the weights highly structured, so a depth-indexed coupled mean-shift update rule can be read off. Figure 1 is a row of three framed panels, each headed by a pastel title chip. Left, Symmetry constraint: an Attention box wrapped in P and P^T circles, with three thumbnails showing the same predictions, the same response to query perturbations and the same influential examples. Middle, Interpretable weights: a noisy weight heatmap and a blocky one joined by an orange block arrow, then the canonical block matrix W. Right, Emergent algorithm: three update equations in a green box, depth read as iterations, and a dot sketch of two groups drifting apart. Flat vector in a draw.io look; only the heatmaps and the scatter are bitmaps.

notes: No paragraph mentions the figure, so roles come from the caption and abstract. The dashed arc over the sandwich is not explained anywhere and is read here only as the layer-to-layer map. X and Y being the feature and label parts follows the abstract (mixed feature-label Gram); blue and red dots as classes is an inference. The prior variant formal-diagram belongs to concept-schematic; finding-cards was chosen for the primary contribution-mosaic.
